title: Kesko Oyj: trade fair companion brief

blocks.text: Kesko is a Finnish trading group (grocery, building and technical trade, car trade) with net sales of €12,474.1m and comparable operating profit of €654.9m in 2025. It is in the middle of two large moves: a €1.2bn acquisition of Dahl's technical trade operations in Sweden, Norway and Denmark, and a proposed €500-700m rights issue to refinance part of the bridge financing, with an EGM on 30 October 2026. Its Q3 2026 interim report is due 29 October 2026. Our angle: ask where manual work will appear when the Dahl units are integrated, and whether efficiency work is competing for attention with the deal itself.

No staff conversation record was supplied. Nothing below states that we have met, spoken with, or agreed anything with anyone at Kesko. Recognising a name in a public photo does not establish a meeting.

items.text: Kesko agreed to acquire Dahl's technical trade operations in Sweden, Norway and Denmark from Saint-Gobain; debt-free price €1.2bn, completion targeted by end-2026.
Kesko plans a €500-700m rights issue to refinance part of the bridge financing for the Dahl acquisition; the EGM on 30 October 2026 is to authorise it. Terms are not yet set.
The European Commission unconditionally approved the Dahl acquisition; completion still depends on other conditions.
Manhattan Associates announced Kesko selected its ActiveWarehouse cloud warehouse solution, with an initial rollout across five distribution centres.
Q2 2026 comparable operating profit rose to €194m; full-year 2026 guidance is narrowed to €670-730m.

blocks.text: Inferred, not confirmed: integrating Dahl's separately branded units may require manual reconciliation of order and financial data. Present this to the client as a question only.

items.text: As the Dahl units come across, which order, invoicing or reporting steps do you expect to stay manual during the first months, and who owns those handoffs?
With the rights issue and the Q3 report coming up, is post-deal efficiency work being planned now, or is it waiting until integration is further along?
Where has the ActiveWarehouse rollout left gaps between warehouse data and the rest of the trading systems, and how are teams bridging them today?

blocks.text: Draft (for a Velho employee to review and send manually)

blocks.label: Intro email
blocks.text:
Hi [Name],

Congratulations on the Dahl deal clearing the Commission. Integrating three Nordic units with their own brands and systems is a lot of moving parts.

We help operations teams find the manual steps that slow integration down and build simple fixes that people actually use. I'm curious whether reconciling orders and finance data across the Dahl units is already on your list, or still ahead.

Would a 20-minute call next week make sense? If the topic isn't relevant right now, I'd still value knowing that.

[Sender]
